products.title: Eden Knit with Pointelle Star - Dark Navy

  • Rib pattern detailing on side body and inner sleeve
  • Raglan shoulder for maximum flexibility and comfort

  • Sounder pointelle star on centre back
  • Machine washable
Product details

We all know that layering is the key to temperature regulation. Air trapped between layers acts as insulation to keep you warm, and then it’s easy to strip off one layer at time when you need to cool off.

At least that’s the theory. The challenge in practice is to layer up without halting the length of your backswing, and without cladding yourself in shiny man-made materials that make you look like you’re heading for Everest base camp.

Which is where our new Eden knit comes in. It’s knitted from a 14-gauge cotton cashmere blend that’s super-soft and naturally breathable. It’s cut to fit nice and snug, with a Raglan sleeve for flexibility across the shoulders, and a flex rib pattern across the side body and inner sleeve. Extended sleeves with thumbholes will keep your hands warm between shots, while the tighter sleeve ensures that there’s no excess fabric to interfere with your grip.

The Eden features Sounder Star embroidery on the chest and pointelle star detailing on the back, is machine-washable, and is perfect for wearing under a polo or jumper, or over a plain white t-shirt or vest.

products.title: Sounder x Protected Species Waterproof Jacket - Olive
products.body_html:
Key features

  • Laser-cut and heat-welded
  • Waterproof YKK zips 
  • Deep pockets with waterproof zip
  • Velcro adjustable cuffs
  • Elasticated adjustable hem
  • Two-year waterproof guarantee
Product details

Waterproofs sound like such a simple idea.

It's just an extra layer than you stuff in your bag if the forecast looks a bit dodgy, and hope that you won't actually need them. If it's just a friendly knock then you can always seek shelter in the clubhouse, watching raindrops run down the windows while you tuck into a Guinness or two.

But when you need to play on through, you need your waterproofs to stand up and deliver. You need to stay dry, but you also need to be able to swing the club. You need to keep the rain off, but also let the sweat out.

The new Sounder waterproof is a proud collaboration with Protected Species, an independent British brand who specialise in performance waterproofs. The founding team have spent their whole careers designing and manufacturing technical apparel for major brands, before setting out to launch Protected Species - building a cult following from customers who value quality, performance and style over garish branding or flashy marketing.

Their fabric is tested to a Waterproof Rating (WR) of 15,000mm/H20/24 - which means its lab-tested by forcing water through a hyrdostatic head for 24 hours. We've also extensively tested the jacket on the course over many months, and are so confident about its performance that the jacket is guaranteed to be waterproof for two years from purchase.

The fabric is  quiet, so you'll get none of that annoying rustle on your backswing. And It's got just enough stretch to accommodate a full-blooded driver swing.

But the fabric is only part of the story. The precision manufacturing process uses lasers so panels fit together perfectly, while all seams are heat-welded. We use high-quality YKK waterproof zips on both the front opening and two deep pockets, while adjustable velcro cuffs and an elasticated hem allow you to create a perfect fit.

Back in 2020, our good friend Sam Cooper and his lovely wife Harriet packed all their belongings and two cocker spaniels into a second-hand camper van and set off on a golfing odyssey - to play every single links golf course in the UK.

Product details

The 425 TP is surely one of the great modern drivers of all time. The legendary 510 TP was so good as a minimal design, but somehow the slightly larger head of the 425 provides a little extra thump. This really is the moment where the full power arrived. No driver since, in spite of the claims, has provided any extra speed. The head shape is great and I had many happy years using this driver. I still will from time to time today. In fact as I write this I’m decided to build another one!

We’ve done a custom paintjob on this one and which matches the legendary Shaqx shaft. This shaft to those who know is held in very high regard. Vijay is rumoured to have used all of his powers of intimidation to snaffle the last few back in 2005. Apparently a few players who were holding onto uncut spares only gave them up after Vijay put their heads into a vice squeeze in the tour van. Stiff mid section and maximum hook resistance clearly vital to his earning capacity.

products.title: The Sounder Golf Bag - Olive / Tan
products.body_html:
Key features
  • Soft grain Italian leather
  • 14oz waxed canvas
  • Two zipped pockets
  • 60cm circumference with leather-bound divider
  • Five stainless steel D-rings
  • Suede padded strap
  • Made in England in small batches
Product details

The Sounder Golf Bag is a project that’s been two years in the making. We could have gone to the same factories in the Far East as everyone else, and got them to make a bag with our logo on it. But then it would have been just another golf bag. And no-one needs just another golf bag.

So instead, we started from scratch, testing every design tweak and every fabric on the course, in all weathers. We found a bespoke factory in England who specialise in working with high-quality leather. We sourced soft grain vegetable-tanned leather from Italy, and combine it with a 14oz waxed canvas to produce a bag that’s durable, lightweight and weather-resistant.

A 60cm circumference metal ring with leather bound divider means that it’s big enough to carry 14 clubs if you’re teeing it up in something serious, but it’s still perfectly-balanced for nine holes with half-set on a Sunday evening. We’ve added two zipped pockets - one for balls, tees and gloves, and one big enough for an extra layer so you won’t get caught short by the weather. High-quality waterproof YKK zips with metal pulls will keep the contents safe and secure. Five stainless steel D-rings provide plenty of options for attaching towels, rangefinders, dog leads or bluetooth speakers.

The result is a single-strap bag that’s comfortable, practical and will age beautifully. It’s a product that we’re proud to put our name on, and we’re confident that it’s a product you will love for many years to come.

Around 2010, Yonex went through a spell of making some serious good stuff.

Ryo Ishikawa was a staff player, and their forgings came out of one of the very best forging houses in Japan. This driver comes from that era - it's a Yonex Ezone 380cc head, with such a perfect pear-shape that I christened the Pear Ulrich Yonexon after one of my favourite Swedes, Per Ulrich Johansson (who is married to Jesper Parnevik's sister - it's a small world, Swedish golf),

It's such a thing of beauty that I figured the only way to do it justice was with a Veylix Arcane 640 t shaft. Sadly I think Veylix are no more, but for a while they made incredibly high-quality shafts with gorgeous paint jobs. This turquiose one turns blue in the sunlight, which is nice.

  • 9.5 degree loft
  • Hzrdous hand-crafted T1100 75 6.0 shaft
  • Lamkin full cord grip with reduced taper

Product details 

Tony Covey from MyGolfSpy once saw me playing with this shaft in my Superquad driver, and said it was like putting whipped cream on a turd. Having only just met him, I was slightly taken aback. But after watching him spray it all over the driving range and then miss every single fairway with his PXG driver I decided to keep my mouth shut - I had it on a string that day and could work it both ways off the tee, and that seemed to be an appropriate response.

Anyhow - the Hzrdous hand-crafted T1100 is one of the best shafts ever made, and it cost me more than $600. Here I've fitted it into an Adams Redline RPM 9.5 degree driver, and given it a slightly wild paint job (thanks to the involvement of our creative director Cathal). Adams made some seriously good stuff back in the day - they were the first manufacturer to add moveable weights to the head, 

The shaft is 45", lie is 57 degrees and swingweight is D2.5.

products.body_html:

  • 15 degree loft
  • Sits 4 degrees open
  • Dynamic Gold X100 shaft
  • Length 42.5"
  • Lie 56 degrees 
  • Lamkin full cord grip with reduced taper
  • Swing weight D4
Product details 

The Titleist 970 is from the brand's golden age, around the year 2000 when Tiger was on staff. Larry Bobka was responsible for making sure the tour guys got whatever they needed, and they weren't tied to what was available at retail - players of that era were much move involved in the process that today's tour players.

This 970 head never came to retail. The players loved the original PT fairway so much, and the 970 is an evolution of that head, with a deeper face and a slightly more compact shape front-to-back. They were so popular on tour that Titleist started paiting them black so they resembled the retail model that they released alongside the 975d drivers.

This one is has 17 degrees of loft, although i've adjusted the face angle so it plays at more like 15 degrees. I've also re-done the paint job, which feels a bit like a crime against such a great club. Sorry.

products.title: Great White Don Blades
products.body_html:
Key features
  • Greg Norman Cobra Blades
  • Completely refurbished by James Day
  • Tour edition Don White forged heads
  • BBF ferules
  • Original satin Project X 6.0 shafts
  • Tour velvet grips with reduced taper under right hand
  • A totally unique one-off set
Product details

I’m certainly not a fan of Greg Norman, I think he’s completely lost his marbles to be honest. He has however always been more clued up than the average pro on the equipment front. He has a decent rack of clubs and retains great clubs from the past. He does some of his own club work like any self respecting connoisseur so maybe he’s not all bad?

These are a rare set of the coveted Greg Norman Cobra blades which he played in the 90s. Cobra made a retail version which I believe came out the Hoffman forge. Norman requested a slightly different version and Cobra enlisted the services of the great Don White at MacGregor. I’m not sure how many sets of these TOUR versions were made but they look quite different up close than the retail versions. They have a longer hosel and very high CG. A rare set of irons which would certainly not be made today, high CG produces low ball flight and sharp zero camber sole grind means there is little to no forgiveness on anything but a perfect strike. Speed is required to get ball flight out of these heads!

I’ve given the heads a polish. I’ve redone the paint fill in what Cathal and I consider to be something far more appealing. BBF ferrules of course and the cherry on the cake? Original satin Project X 6.0 shafts. Try finding a set of these on ebay! The original Project X was at one time in the early 2000s used by the majority of the world’s top 10. It presented a major issue for the manufacturers due to the high cost. At wholesale it cost five times the price of other steel shafts. The solution came in cynical form sadly. True Temper simply bought Precision Golf Shafts who made them, shut them down and then made the cheap version we see today. I kept a few sets on ice but sadly this is my last set. Tour Velvet grips installed properly of course with reduced taper under the right hand.

See build sheet for specs but the usual irrational tolerances are in play. Progressive swing weight/MOI provides set matching and feel you only get from the very best club builders.

products.title: Aussie Rules
products.body_html:
Key features
  • Tad Moore Maxfli Australian Blades
  • 4-PW
  • Project X LS shafts
  • Lambkin Crossline Cord Grip with Reduced Taper
  • Custom paint job 
  • BBF ferules
Product details

Any fan of great forged blades should be a fan of the Maxfli Australian blade. These beauties when through lots of iterations from the late sixties until this set, which was the last forged iron made by Maxfli, back in 1996.

Here's what Tad Moore, one of the all-time great clubmakers, said when he worked at Maxfli during the nineties.

"These irons were made at Hoffman Foundry just outside Memphis. They were very good to work with. The original heads I made at the tour shop in Kobe Japan offices of Dunlop Japan. I was asked in 1990 to develop irons, wedges and make a few persimmon drivers. All these were made in that great shop. I then transferred iron head masters to Hoffman. The drivers were all made in Japan. I had one Tour win with David Frost. Enjoy these irons... they are sweet!"

I honestly believe that the shape of these heads can't be beaten - they are just perfect, and beautiful to look at. They have traditional lofts and relatively light heads, so I had to to build them with longer shafts - the six iron is a standard length but with the loft of a seven irons. You'll be hitting more club than your pals using modern jacked lofts, but check your ego at the door and enjoy the sensation of playing with real blades.

I debated how to build these, but in the end I settled on my personal spec - these are too pretty for me to resist taking them onto the cause. The paint fill and BBF ferrules follow the Aussie theme.

products.body_html:

  • Diamana Blue Board 93 x shaft

Product details 

There is an art to making a great five wood. Sadly, the big golf manufacturers gave up on art a long time ago.

This Sonartec SS07 is the best five wood you will ever experience. I've added about eight grams of head weight, bent the head to flatten the lie and to make it sit more open. The shaft is a Diamana Blue Board 93 x - the classic fairway wood shaft, and the one that Tiger used until they ran out. It's short and heavy, just like a five wood should be.

The custom paint job makes it feel like a Ford Granada from 1982.

products.title: The Stealth Bomber
products.body_html:
Key features
  • Taylor Made Superquad Tour Issue ‘282’ driver
  • Graphite Design XC 7 x shaft
  • Lamkin Crossline Cord Ribbed grip with reduced taper
  • The best driver head of all time?
  • It just might be you know...
Product details 

The best driver head of all time? This one is in the mix.

How can this be? If we believe what we're told, every new model of every new driver goes further than the one before, which means we should all be hitting the ball 600 yards by now.

The truth is that since 2004, all driver heads have been right on the limit for ball speed off the clubface. Ever since, the manufacturers have added no end of adjustable cogs and weights to justify their ever-increasing prices - with little attention to how it sits, or whether players can hit different shots with it.

I prefer something more minimal, and the classic 282 head is exactly that. In fact, I daren't talk about why they are so good because it will just increase the prices that they fetch on eBay, and I'm building a stockpile so I've got a steady supply when the nuclear apocalypse arrives.

I play a Superquad 282 in my optimum set - this is your chance to own one too.

Product details

The Silver Bullet is a cocktail comprising two staples of the British golf club - 50ml of gin, 30ml of Kummel. A couple of these really cuts through the long lunch with unlimited Claret, setting you up for the afternoon round. And for your opening tee shot, this is a club with a similar degree of potency.

The whole Sonartec story is one for another day. But rest assured, these ARE the best fairway woods ever made. I have made a personal commitment to acquire enough Sonartec heads to see out my days, an obsession that's beginning to rival my collection of Footjoy Classics.

The SS3.5 was one of the last models - a deep face, perfect shape and an absolute rocket launcher. Unfortunately I find that many of these heads never quite sit correctly, often sitting closed at address. Rest assured that this has been rectified and this now sits absolutely square.

We've done a custom paint job on this one, and paired with a prototype tour-only Project x Graphite shaft. Please see spec sheet for all the details.

products.body_html:

  • Knitted shaft

Product details

You’d be surprised at just how hard it is to make the perfect headcover.

The sizing has to be perfect - just tight enough to fully protect the head, with enough elasticity that you can slip it on and off with a satisfying pull.

We could have just gone to a factory in China and asked them to stick a Sounder logo onto one of their standard models. But then it would have been just another head cover - and nobody needs just another head cover.

So after (literally) years of prototyping and testing on the course, we settled on a classic design with the head made from a high-quality sherpa fleece, and a sleeve made from a soft acrylic knit that’s long enough to protect the shaft.

We used tough cord to create a sturdy pull loop, added a Sounder word mark patch and a Play Well mantra tab - a reminder to enjoy the moment every time you unleash the timber.  Available in two sizes - the Driver fits a modern 460cc head, while the Fairway version is designed for a standard 3 wood or 5 wood.

products.body_html:

Product details

As part of our proud association with The Cleeve Hill Festival of Golf, we've worked with our very talented friend Joe McDonnell to create a unique piece of art to celebrate this unique golf course.

Joe's work is created through his command of multiple disciplines - starting with a drone survey of the land, which is then brought to life through photogrammetry, 3D sculpting and digital watercolour painting techniques.

The course at Cleeve Hill takes the golfer on a journey across Cleeve Common - climbing from the clubhouse to the highest point in the Cotswolds, taking in heroic carries over long-since abandoned quarries and navigating the ramparts of a 3,000-year-old Iron Age fort. There's nowhere else quite like it, and Joe's original methodology captures the spirit of Cleeve in a way that no ordinary photograph or painting can do.

The glicee print is available framed or unframed. Both options are printed on museum-grade Hahnemühle Photo Rag paper, with the framed version mounted on a premium white board and finished in a white wooden frame.

Find out more about Joe's work at joemcdgolf.com

products.title: The Sounder x Grenson Golf Shoe - White
products.body_html:
Key features
  • Limited-edition Grenson collaboration 
  • Hand-made in Northampton
  • White calf Italian leather upper
  • Fully lined uncoated beige calf leather
  • Off white suede and Sounder star
  • Navy French calf leather back tag
  • Leather sole with pre-drilled screw in cleats
  • Goodyear welted construction
Product details

We always wanted to add a golf shoe to the Sounder collection. And when the time came, we knew exactly who we wanted to work with - the amazing team at Grenson, an independent British shoemaker based in Northamptonshire, where they have been making shoes by hand for more than 150 years.

After more than a year in development, we couldn't be prouder to launch the Sounder x Grenson golf shoe - a limited-edition collaboration and a unique opportunity to own what's sure to become a collectors' item.

The shoe is based on Grenson’s 201 G-Fit last, which has a generous rounded toe shape for a classic shape, and extra toe spring for comfort. The upper is white Italian calf leather, with an off-white suede and Sounder star, and a Navy back tag made from French calf leather. The shoe is fully lined with naturally wicking uncoated beige calf leather.

The shoes are leather soled with pre-drilled screw-in cleats, with a 3mm rubber midsole, and a Goodyear welted construction. They are as comfortable to wear as they are beautiful to look at, and have been road-tested in all weathers and turf conditions - not least on our summer trip to the world-famous links of Machrihanish.

Each pair of shoes are made by hand in the Grenson workshop in Northampton. The shoe is available in half sizes from size 8 to 13. Your shoes will be shipped in a Grenson shoe box, with a unique Sounder shoe bag made from offcuts of the garment-dyed cotton we use to make our bestselling Good Walk Chino range.

We know that the £495 price isn't cheap, and might not be for everyone. But these hand-made leather-soled shoes are a truly special collaboration, and something that we know will bring the owner great joy for many years to come.
